content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Convert between moles and mass fluently
Apply the n = m/M formula to various problems
Converting between moles and mass is one of the most important skills in chemistry. This lesson provides extensive practice with the formula $n = \frac{m}{M}$ and its rearrangements.
Write the formula: m = n × M
Calculate the number of moles in 4.6 g of sodium (Na, Ar = 23).
Calculate the number of moles in 8.8 g of carbon dioxide (CO₂).
How many moles are in 49 g of sulfuric acid (H₂SO₄)?
Calculate the moles in 14.8 g of calcium hydroxide (Ca(OH)₂).
Calculate the mass of 3 mol of magnesium oxide (MgO).
What is the mass of 0.25 mol of copper sulfate (CuSO₄)?
Calculate the mass of 0.1 mol of glucose (C₆H₁₂O₆).
0.25 mol of a compound has a mass of 15 g. Calculate its molar mass.
4.4 g of a gas contains 0.1 mol. What is the Mr of the gas?
What mass of calcium chloride (CaCl₂) contains the same number of moles as 4 g of sodium hydroxide (NaOH)?
Step 2: Find mass of 0.1 mol CaCl₂
How many oxygen atoms are in 8 g of sulfur dioxide (SO₂)?
1 mol SO₂ contains 2 mol O atoms
Always calculate Mr from the formula before using n = m/M
Dividing when you should multiply (or vice versa)
Check: moles = mass ÷ Mr; mass = moles × Mr
Always check the Periodic Table for Ar values
Always include units: mol for moles, g for mass
Calculate the number of moles in:
a) 9.2 g of sodium (Ar = 23) (1 mark) b) 7.1 g of chlorine gas, Cl₂ (1 mark) c) 10 g of calcium carbonate, CaCO₃ (2 marks) d) 53 g of sodium carbonate, Na₂CO₃ (2 marks)
a) 0.5 mol of carbon (1 mark) b) 2.5 mol of water, H₂O (2 marks) c) 0.04 mol of copper(II) sulfate, CuSO₄ (2 marks) d) 0.2 mol of ethanol, C₂H₅OH (2 marks)
A compound has a molar mass of 58 g/mol. What mass of this compound contains 0.05 mol? (2 marks)
11 g of a compound contains 0.25 mol. Calculate the Mr of the compound. (2 marks)
What mass of magnesium hydroxide, Mg(OH)₂, contains the same number of moles as 8 g of sodium hydroxide, NaOH? (3 marks)
How many hydrogen atoms are present in 4.5 g of water? (4 marks)
The unit of amount of substance
Sum of relative atomic masses in a formula
The formula relating moles, mass, and molar mass
To find moles: divide mass by molar mass
To find mass: multiply moles by molar mass
Always calculate Mr first from the chemical formula
Include correct units in all calculations
